title: Marguerite and the Letter Revisited
premise: In the waning days of the Republic of Valcourt, Ivo Joubert carried sealed dispatches through a collapsing war and vanished into the fishing town of Sainte-Marine, trading a courier's name for a fisherman's silence. Fifteen years later, the new Empire's army requisitions the town and seizes the harbor ledger — the one document listing every soul who sheltered republican couriers, including Ivo and the family of Marguerite Delac, the woman Ivo promised to protect and who is now declared an enemy of the state. As the requisitioned troopship prepares to sail on the morning tide carrying both the ledger and Marguerite's daughter as a hostage-guest of the Empire, Ivo must break fifteen years of careful invisibility: forge, steal, or confess their way aboard, and decide whether a promise made in peacetime outweighs the safety of everyone who helped them hide. The story ends with Ivo trading the last undelivered republican cipher — their final proof of innocence — to a sympathetic imperial clerk in exchange for striking the names from the ledger, sailing out with Marguerite's family on the morning tide, stateless but no longer alone.
about_author: Jonah Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging seized civil records in coastal municipal libraries, where the margins of ledgers told truer stories than the entries. This is their third novel, all concerned with people history recorded only in passing.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet Water
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Fifteen years after the republic fell, Ivo mends nets in Sainte-Marine, practicing the small disciplines of invisibility: no letters, no opinions, no past. A child asks where Ivo learned to read tide-tables, and Ivo deflects. Emotional beat: the ache of a life lived in the conditional tense.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, via her letters kept in Ivo's sea chest. Flashback to the last diplomatic mission: Marguerite, a translator, entrusting Ivo with a promise — that her family would always have a door. Present-day Marguerite writes that the Empire's surveyors have come to count boats, and names. Emotional beat: dread arriving in polite handwriting.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Imperial officers post the requisition order: the harbor, the granary, the troopship Corvane, and all municipal records. The town ledger is carted off to the customs house. Ivo watches their own alias — 'Ivo Joubert, fisherman, arrived 15 years ago, origin unknown' — disappear into a soldier's satchel. Emotional beat: the illusion of safety cracking.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Knows
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo catalogs from memory what the ledger exposes: the false arrival date, the harbor fees paid in old republican coin, the entry for 'Delac, dependents, three.' Old friend Bastien warns Ivo to run before the audit. Ivo refuses — the Delacs are still in town. Emotional beat: fear transmuting into obligation.

chapters.title: Enemy Blood
chapters.summary: Marguerite's daughter Solène's POV, age nineteen. Soldiers post the proscription list; the Delac name is on it. Neighbors who traded bread yesterday suddenly cannot see her. Solène comes to the one person her mother's letters called 'a friend of the republic.' Emotional beat: the vertigo of becoming invisible to everyone but a stranger.

chapters.title: The Promise, Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo shows Solène Marguerite's last letter and the promise it contains. Solène is furious — fifteen years of silence, while her mother waited for word that never came. Ivo cannot defend the silence except to say it kept people safe, and Solène asks: safe like her mother? Emotional beat: guilt meeting grief, neither yielding.

chapters.title: The Customs House
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, scouting. Ivo poses as a boatwright summoned to assess the Corvane and sees the ledgers stacked in the clerk's office, and learns the ship sails on the morning tide in nine days — carrying troops, records, and 'proscribed dependents' for trial on the mainland. Emotional beat: the clock starting.

chapters.title: Bastien's Bargain
chapters.summary: Bastien's POV. Bastien, who has spent fifteen years cultivating the imperial harbor-master with wine and flattery, offers to get Ivo aboard as a contracted pilot — but only Ivo, one name, one berth. Ivo must choose between their own escape and the Delacs. Emotional beat: friendship strained by arithmetic.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo teaches Solène to move like someone with nothing to hide: how to be dull, forgettable, unremarkable. Solène proves better at it than Ivo ever was. They map the customs house guard rotations using Bastien's gossip. Emotional beat: two fugitives becoming, reluctantly, a team.

chapters.title: The Cipher in the Keel
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, flashback. The last undelivered dispatch of the republic: a cipher book sewn into a ship's keel, which Ivo recovered and has kept hidden for fifteen years — the one object that could prove Ivo was a loyal courier, not a collaborator. Emotional beat: the cost of loyalty measured in what it forbids you to show.

chapters.title: A Clerk Named Ferrand
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo studies the junior customs clerk Ferrand: young, meticulous, visibly uneasy about the 'dependents' order. Ivo engineers a small kindness — returning Ferrand's dropped commission papers unopened — and watches the clerk's suspicion soften into something like curiosity. Emotional beat: trust as a slow, deliberate craft.

chapters.title: Solène's Mistake
chapters.summary: Solène's POV. Solène, trying to slip a message to a detained Delac cousin, is nearly caught by the garrison. Ivo covers for her at real risk, and afterward the argument they've been avoiding erupts: Ivo's silence versus Solène's recklessness, both the same wound. Emotional beat: anger revealing kinship.

chapters.title: The Harbor-Master's Dinner
chapters.summary: Bastien's POV. Bastien secures Ivo a pilot's contract for the Corvane's sailing, but at dinner the harbor-master mentions, casually, that the records will be verified against passenger lists — and that discrepancies will be tried on the mainland. Bastien realizes what he's helped set in motion. Emotional beat: complicity curdling.

chapters.title: What Silence Bought
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, flashback to the war's end. The night Marguerite was arrested by the republic's own secret police, and Ivo — carrying her exoneration letter — arrived too late, and chose silence over testimony to protect the network. Fifteen years of quiet built on that one failure. Emotional beat: the true origin of the promise.

chapters.title: Ferrand's Question
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ferrand, auditing the ledger, finds the impossible: Ivo Joubert's arrival date predates any fishing license. He summons Ivo privately — not to accuse, but to ask why a man with no past would risk it for proscribed strangers. Ivo tells him the truth, or the shape of it. Emotional beat: confession as gambit.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ferrand reveals the records will be burned after boarding — no, worse, forwarded — and that he has discretion over 'clerical errors.' Ivo offers the cipher book: proof that Ferrand's own father, a republican clerk, was exonerated by a courier's testimony that never arrived. The price: strike the Delac and Joubert entries. Emotional beat: two inheritances of silence, bartered.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Granary
chapters.summary: Solène's POV. A neighbor denounces the Delac hiding place. Solène and her grandmother are taken to the customs house to be held aboard the Corvane overnight. Ivo, watching from the crowd, must do nothing — a pilot cannot be a rescuer. Emotional beat: the promise breaking in public.

chapters.title: Night Boarding
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, climax begins. Ivo uses the pilot's berth to board the Corvane before dawn, finds the Delacs in the hold, and — with Ferrand's forged correction slip — moves them onto the passenger manifest as contracted harbor laborers, a category no one audits twice. Emotional beat: fifteen years of caution spent in a single hour.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, climax. At the gangway, the harbor-master cross-examines Ivo's papers; Bastien, drunk and loyal, vouches with a lie that could hang him. The Corvane casts off with the Delacs aboard and the ledger's relevant pages, thanks to Ferrand, quietly misfiled. Emotional beat: terror and triumph indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Open Water
chapters.summary: Solène's POV. Aboard, Solène confronts the reality: they are free of Sainte-Marine and of everything — home, country, name. Ivo finally tells her the whole truth about her mother's arrest and the letter that came too late. Solène grieves, then chooses: 'Then we stop waiting.' Emotional beat: grief converting into forward motion.

chapters.title: The Undelivered Letter
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In the Corvane's wake, Ivo writes the letter that should have been written fifteen years ago — to Marguerite, wherever she is — and gives it to Solène to carry, the promise transferred rather than fulfilled. Bastien's farewell note, smuggled aboard, arrives with the pilot's pay. Emotional beat: release of the oldest debt.

chapters.title: Marguerite and the Letter, Revisited
chapters.summary: Alternating Ivo and Solène POV, coda. In a neutral port, the Delacs and Ivo take a small house with a door that faces the sea — a door kept visibly open. Solène begins teaching letters to harbor children, including a clerk's son with Ferrand's careful handwriting. Ivo, named at last and unafraid, signs a document: Ivo Joubert, courier, retired. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not granted.
